events.title: Rob Pike and Ken Thompson design UTF-8
events.summary: Rob Pike and Ken Thompson designed UTF-8 in September 1992 at Bell Labs — the variable-width encoding underlying the modern web; Plan 9 converted within days and a formal paper followed later.
events.about: UTF-8 let ASCII-compatible systems handle Unicode without breaking existing software. Every API, database, and browser today assumes UTF-8 as the default string encoding.

narrative.whyChosen: UTF-8 is the universal text encoding of the internet.
narrative.whyImportant: It enabled global software without abandoning ASCII infrastructure.
narrative.problemSolved: Fixed-width Unicode encodings wasted space and broke Unix text tools.

events.title: ODBC 1.0 released
events.summary: Microsoft and partners shipped the Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) SDK in September 1992 — a standard C API for talking to SQL databases.
events.about: ODBC let one Windows app query Oracle, SQL Server, and Access through the same driver interface — the pattern JDBC followed for Java and every ORM still abstracts today. It made client/server database apps portable across vendors.

narrative.whyChosen: ODBC standardized how applications connect to relational databases.
narrative.whyImportant: Driver-based database access became the default integration model for decades.
narrative.problemSolved: Each database shipped a proprietary C API; apps were locked to one vendor.
